references.text: Explains the Jubilee year mentioned in the verse, when all Hebrew slaves were to be freed and return to their property.
Elaborates on how an Israelite who has sold himself is to be treated as a hired worker and not as a slave, and calculates the time until the Jubilee year.
Earlier law regarding Hebrew slaves who were to serve for six years and be released in the seventh, a parallel to service until the Jubilee year.
Repeats the laws concerning the release of Hebrew slaves and commands that they must not be sent away empty-handed.
The immediate context forbids treating a poor Israelite as a slave, but rather as a hired worker or a foreigner.
Refers to the law's command to free Hebrew slaves after seven years, and criticizes Israel for breaking this covenant.
Job compares human life to the service of a hired worker, using the same terminology applied to the poor Israelite.
